subject: Post-demo: NimbleAI latency & throughput readout + next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nimbleai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: NimbleAI latency & throughput readout + next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the candid run-through of your production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the bench.

Recap of what we saw:
- Typical user request shape: 512 tokens prompt, ~64 token generations (avg).
- Your current hyperscaler setup hits p95 ~420ms and p99 ~880ms for the 256→320 windup case; throughput reported ~120 tokens/sec per GPU for the baseline model.
- Primary goals you called out: consistent p95 under 350ms and stable p99 under 700ms during peak.

What Redwood proposes for the A/B bench:
1) A (Baseline): your current hyperscaler endpoint (we'll reproduce with your trace/trace-like workload).
2) B (Redwood-opt): Redwood running the same model on our optimized runtime + quant profile with KV prefix caching on identical GPU class.
Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail error rate, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, memory per-request, and cost/tokens.

Attached is a lightweight AB test matrix (ab-test-matrix.csv) with proposed run cadence (short warmup, three 10-minute runs at different concurrency levels). If this looks good we'll schedule access windows — ideally Wed/Thu next week.

Requested from you to run the bench:
- Long-running trace or representative sample of ~2k requests (we can also syntheticize if preferred)
- Preferred test window(s) and whether procurement needs to approve any infra access

Proposed sales timeline / next customer-facing milestones:
- August 31: finalize test matrix + sign brief POC scope
- Sept 7–9: run bench and deliver readout (p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost delta)
- Sept 14: decision checkpoint (go/no-go on Dedicated eval)

Let me know if you'd rather define different p95/p99 targets — I put down what you mentioned on the call.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: ab-test-matrix.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nimbleai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbleai.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NimbleAI latency & throughput readout + next steps

Aditya — thanks for the solid summary and for putting together the matrix. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- We can provide a 2k request trace by EOD Tuesday.
- Procurement looped in here — they need an SOW/PO template for POC infra access. How heavy is the access? Do we need any cross-account role?
- For the A/B runs: can you commit to the same GPU class (A100 40GB) on both sides? We need apples-to-apples.

Targets are correct; curious how Redwood handles prefix caching with multi-user workloads (we run mixed-length prompts). Also: how will you measure tokens/sec — per-GPU or aggregated?

If you can send a short SOW and confirm the GPU parity, we'll start procurement review.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
CTO, NimbleAI
sanjay@nimbleai.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NimbleAI latency & throughput readout + next steps

Adding a quick internal ops checklist so we can respond to Sanjay without back-and-forth:

- Confirm GPU parity: yes, we can provision A100 40GB for the Redwood run; cost note in the SOW.
- AB test definitions: See row details in ab-test-matrix.csv — we should include two concurrency tiers: 8 and 24 concurrent requests to match their expected peak envelope.
- Prefix caching behavior: Redwood will simulate multi-tenant mixed-length traffic; caching policy will be described in the readout (hits, misses, and eviction stats). We'll also capture per-request KV cache hit flag so we can filter metrics.
- Tokens/sec: capture both per-GPU tokens/sec and aggregate across the pool; provide normalization to tokens/sec per $ to show unit economics.
- Data access: we will insist logs only for benchmarking (no persisted customer data) — add line in SOW.

I'll draft a tight POC SOW (1 page) and a short risk/ops note for procurement. Monica — can you pull typical token-length distribution from our PROD traces to include as a comparison baseline?

Thanks — will aim to circulate the SOW + a one-page bench runbook by end of day Tuesday.

— Lauren
Director, Bench Ops, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Sanjay — looping back with the two deliverables we discussed.

1) Short SOW / POC scope (attached: MAL-POC-scope.pdf) — includes: scope, access model (read-only trace ingest), A100 parity note, test windows, acceptance criteria (p95 < 350ms AND p99 < 700ms for the 256→320 sketch), and data handling clause.

2) AB test runbook (attached as spreadsheet earlier: ab-test-matrix.csv) — outlines warmup, steady-state duration, concurrency tiers (8 / 24), and measurement windows.

Quoted from your last message: 
> For the A/B runs: can you commit to the same GPU class (A100 40GB) on both sides? We need apples-to-apples.

Yes — we will provision A100 40GB for the Redwood side. We'll annotate any kernel/quantization differences in the readout so it's clear what contributes to delta. Tokens/sec will be reported both per-GPU and aggregated; we'll normalize to tokens/sec per $ and include a small table showing cost assumptions.

Requested next items from you:
- Send the 2k request trace (or confirm synthetic) by Tue EOD (your timezone).
- Procurement: please confirm who will review the one-page SOW and estimated timeline for approval. If DocuSign makes it faster we can send the SOW that route.

Proposed schedule (re-confirming):
- Tue Aug 31: SOW signed / trace provided
- Wed–Thu Sep 1–2: bench runs (short windows)
- Tue Sep 7: readout and results deck (p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost delta, recommended follow-up)

If that works, I'll send the DocuSign link to Procurement and schedule the bench windows.

Thanks,
Aditya
